questions.question_text: How many hours of pre-license education does Wisconsin require for a salesperson license?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin requires 72 hours of REEB-approved pre-license education for salesperson licensure. Alternatively, candidates may complete 10 semester-hour credits in real estate or real estate law from an accredited institution.

questions.question_text: A candidate completed 10 semester credits in real estate law at a university 5 years ago. Can they use these credits for licensure?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, the 10-credit path has no recency limit
distractors: No, all pre-license education must be within 4 years
No, only the 72-hour course satisfies the requirement
Yes, but only if the school is REEB-approved
questions.explanation: The 4-year recency limit applies to par. (a) only, the 72-hour REEB 25.033 course (Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.013 (1)). Par. (b), the 10-semester-credit path at an accredited institution of higher education, carries no time limit, so 5-year-old credits still qualify.

questions.question_text: What is the alternative to completing 72 hours of REEB-approved pre-license education?
questions.correct_answer: 10 semester credits in real estate or real estate law
distractors: A bachelor's degree in any field
5 years of real estate work experience
questions.explanation: Wisconsin offers two paths under REEB 12.013 (1): 72 hours of REEB-approved pre-license education completed within 4 years of licensure, OR 10 semester-hour credits in real estate or real estate law from an accredited institution, which has no recency limit.

questions.question_text: Within how many years of licensure must a candidate complete the 72-hour pre-license course?
questions.explanation: The 72-hour REEB 25.033 course must be completed within 4 years of licensure (Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.013 (1) (a)). The alternative 10-semester-credit path under par. (b) has no time limit at all.

questions.question_text: Which topic is NOT typically covered in Wisconsin's 72-hour pre-license curriculum?
questions.explanation: The 72-hour salesperson curriculum covers real property, the real estate business, ownership and land description, agency, contracts, financing, valuation, fair housing, environmental law, closings, and Wisconsin license law (Wis. Admin. Code REEB 25.033). Commercial investment analysis is not part of it.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum age to obtain a Wisconsin real estate salesperson license?
questions.explanation: No action may be taken on any application from an applicant under 18 (Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.01 (7)). Age is the only personal-eligibility bar — Wisconsin has no high school diploma, GED, or citizenship requirement for a real estate license.

questions.question_text: A license candidate has completed pre-license education. What exam must they pass?
distractors: The National Association of REALTORS exam
questions.explanation: Wisconsin contracts with Pearson VUE to develop and administer the licensing examination. The salesperson exam is a single 140-question Wisconsin exam with no separate national portion, and passing is a scaled score of 75 on a 0-100 scale.

questions.question_text: An applicant with a criminal record applies for a salesperson license. Which statement is correct?
questions.correct_answer: Only crimes substantially related to real estate may affect eligibility
distractors: Any criminal conviction is an automatic disqualifier
Criminal history is not considered at all
Only felonies within the last 5 years matter
questions.explanation: Conviction of an offense whose circumstances substantially relate to real estate practice is a ground for discipline (Wis. Stat. s. 452.14 (3) (p)), and an initial license is separately barred after a felony until at least 3 years past release, subject to a board suitability determination (s. 452.25 (1)). Not every conviction disqualifies an applicant.

questions.question_text: What score is required to pass the Wisconsin real estate salesperson exam?
questions.correct_answer: A scaled score of 75 on a 0-100 scale
distractors: 75% on a national portion and 75% on a state portion
questions.explanation: Wisconsin's salesperson exam is a single 140-question Wisconsin exam with no separate national portion. Pearson VUE equates the exam forms and reports a scaled score on a 0-100 scale; DSPS set the passing score at 75. A 75 is not the same as answering 75% of the questions correctly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a requirement for a Wisconsin real estate salesperson license?
distractors: A high school diploma or GED
U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residence
Sponsorship by a currently licensed broker
questions.explanation: The only personal-eligibility bar is age: the applicant must be at least 18 (Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.01 (7)). Wisconsin has no high school diploma, GED, or citizenship requirement. The remaining requirements are education (72 hours or 10 semester credits), passing the Pearson VUE exam, and the Wis. Stat. s. 452.25 (1) felony review.

questions.question_text: How many total hours of continuing education must Wisconsin licensees complete per biennium?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin requires 18 hours of CE per two-year licensing period: 12 hours of mandatory courses plus 6 hours of elective courses. Electives must be Wisconsin-specific.

questions.question_text: Of the 18 CE hours required, how many must be mandatory versus elective courses?
questions.explanation: The 18-hour CE requirement breaks down into 12 mandatory hours and 6 elective hours. Elective courses must be Wisconsin-specific, covering WI forms, law, or administrative code.

questions.question_text: A salesperson takes an elective CE course on general negotiation skills with no Wisconsin content. Does this satisfy the elective requirement?
distractors: Yes, if the course is at least 3 hours
No, electives can only cover fair housing
questions.explanation: Wisconsin CE electives must include instruction on Wisconsin forms, Wisconsin law, Wisconsin administrative code, or a combination of these topics. A generic negotiation course would not qualify.

questions.question_text: A salesperson obtains their license on November 1 of an even-numbered year. Must they complete CE for that biennium?
questions.correct_answer: No, they are exempt for that biennium
distractors: Yes, they must complete all 18 hours
Yes, but only 9 hours are required
No, but they must complete 6 elective hours
questions.explanation: A person who receives an original salesperson's license after October 1 in an even year is exempt from the CE requirement for that biennium (Wis. Admin. Code REEB 25.065 (5)). The exemption is salesperson-only; a newly licensed broker must still complete CE.

questions.question_text: What is the renewal deadline for Wisconsin real estate licenses?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin real estate licenses expire on December 14 of even-numbered years. The next renewal deadline is December 14, 2026. All 18 CE hours must be completed before this date.

questions.question_text: A licensed salesperson wants to open their own real estate firm. What additional license type is required?
questions.correct_answer: A broker license and a firm license
distractors: Only a firm license is needed
Only a broker license is needed
A managing agent license from DSPS
questions.explanation: To operate a firm the individual needs a broker license and the business entity needs its own. Under Wis. Stat. s. 452.12 (2) (a) a broker's license may be issued to a business entity if the entity has at least one business representative licensed as a broker.

questions.question_text: How much is the biennial license renewal fee for a Wisconsin real estate salesperson?
questions.explanation: The biennial renewal fee for a Wisconsin real estate license is $60. A $25 late fee applies if the renewal is submitted after the December 14 deadline.

questions.question_text: To qualify for a broker license, how many years of salesperson experience are required?
questions.explanation: A broker applicant must practice as a licensed salesperson under a broker's direct supervision for at least 2 years within the last 4 years, and the experience must total at least 40 points: 5 per closed residential transaction, 10 per commercial, 0.5 per month per property management contract, and 1 per time share (Wis. Stat. s. 452.09 (4) (a) 1.; REEB 12.017 (3) (a)).

questions.question_text: A salesperson fails to renew by December 14. What must they do to continue practicing?
questions.correct_answer: Renew late with the standard fee plus a $25 late fee
distractors: Retake the licensing exam before renewal
Complete an additional 18 hours of CE courses
Reapply as a new licensee from scratch
questions.explanation: Late renewal requires the $60 renewal fee plus the $25 late fee under Wis. Stat. s. 440.08 (3) (a). No re-examination is required, but s. 452.12 (5) (b) bars the licensee from engaging in any activity covered by the license until the renewal is granted.

questions.question_text: A salesperson submits their renewal 10 days after the December 14 deadline. What additional cost applies?
distractors: No additional fee for late renewal
questions.explanation: Late renewals incur a $25 fee in addition to the standard $60 renewal fee, making the total $85. Licensees should renew before December 14 of even-numbered years to avoid this penalty.
